questions: How do I apply for admission?
How can I take admission in this college?
entries.answer:
Admissions are handled online:

1. Register on the college admission portal
2. Fill in the application form and upload your marksheets and ID proof
3. Pay the application fee
4. Wait for the merit list, then attend document verification and counselling

You can track your application status from the same portal.

questions: What is the eligibility criteria for B.Tech?
What marks are required for admission?
Minimum percentage required to get admission
entries.answer: For B.Tech you need a pass in Class 12 with Physics and Mathematics plus Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science or a technical subject, with the minimum aggregate set by the university. A valid entrance exam score is considered where applicable. The exact cut-offs are published each year on the Admissions page.

questions: Which documents are required for admission?
What certificates do I need to submit?
What should I carry for counselling?
entries.answer:
Keep these ready, both originals and photocopies:

- Class 10 and Class 12 marksheets
- Entrance exam scorecard
- Transfer or migration certificate
- Government ID proof
- Passport size photographs
- Category certificate, if applicable

questions: Last date to apply for admission
entries.answer: Admission dates are announced on the official website every year. Applications usually open early in the admission cycle and close before counselling begins. Please check the Admissions page for the current schedule.

questions: How do I get a scholarship?
Is there any financial aid for students?
entries.answer: Merit-based scholarships are offered on the basis of entrance rank and academic performance, and need-based aid is available for eligible students. Apply through the scholarship section of the student portal with income and marks documents. The scholarship cell can confirm the current criteria.

questions: How much are the tuition fees?
What is the cost of the B.Tech program?
How much do I have to pay for the course?
entries.answer: Tuition depends on the program and is listed in the official fee notice on the website. It is paid semester-wise or annually. Hostel, mess and examination fees are charged separately. The accounts office can share the latest fee sheet for your program.

questions: How can I pay my fees?
Can I pay fees by UPI?
Can I pay fees by cash or demand draft?
entries.answer: Fees can be paid online through the student portal using UPI, net banking, debit or credit card. Offline payment is accepted at the accounts office by demand draft. Always keep the payment receipt, as it is needed for hostel and exam registration.

questions: What is the last date to pay fees?
What if I miss the fee deadline?
entries.answer: The last date for each semester is announced on the notice board and the portal. Payments after the due date attract a late fee, and registration for the semester can be held until dues are cleared. If you have a genuine problem, apply to the accounts office before the deadline.

questions: Can I get a refund if I withdraw my admission?
How do I cancel admission and get my money back?
Refund if I leave the college
entries.answer: If you withdraw your admission, a refund is processed as per the university refund schedule, which depends on how early you withdraw. Submit a written withdrawal request with your fee receipt to the accounts office. Some charges, such as the application fee, are non-refundable.

questions: Can I pay fees in installments?
Is there an installment option for fees?
Can I pay fees in two parts?
entries.answer: Semester-wise payment is the default. For other installment arrangements, submit a request to the accounts office before the due date and they will tell you what is allowed in your case.

questions: Is the library open on Sunday?
What time does the library close?
Is the library open on weekends?
entries.answer: The central library is open from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, Monday to Saturday, and from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM on Sundays. Hours are extended during exam weeks.

questions: How many books can I borrow?
How long can I keep a library book?
How do I issue a book?
entries.answer: Students can issue up to 3 books at a time for 14 days using their ID card, and can renew once if no one else has reserved the book. Reference books and journals stay in the library.

questions: What is the late fine for library books?
What if I lose a library book?
I returned my book late, what is the fine?
entries.answer: A small per-day fine is charged on overdue books. If you lose a book, you must replace it with the same edition or pay its current price plus a processing charge. Report it to the librarian as early as possible.

questions: Can I read research papers from my hostel?
entries.answer: Yes. The library subscribes to e-books and online journals, which you can use from the campus network or through remote access with your student login. Ask at the library help desk to activate your account.

questions: What facilities are available in the hostel?
What is available in the hostel rooms?
Is there wifi and laundry in the hostel?
entries.answer: Hostels provide furnished rooms, Wi-Fi, a mess, laundry, common rooms, a reading hall, power backup and round-the-clock security with a warden on duty.

questions: How do I apply for the hostel?
How do I get a hostel room?
When can I apply for a hostel room?
entries.answer: Hostel applications open after admission confirmation. Rooms are allotted on a first-come basis, so apply early through the student portal and pay the hostel fee to confirm your seat.

questions: What time do the hostel gates close?
Can I come back late to the hostel?
entries.answer: The curfew is 10 PM on weekdays. For late returns or special permission, inform the warden in advance.

questions: How much does the hostel cost?
How much do I have to pay for the hostel?
entries.answer: Hostel fees depend on the room type and are listed in the fee notice. Mess charges are billed separately. The hostel office can share the current rates.

questions: Can my parents visit the hostel?
Are guests allowed in the hostel?
entries.answer: Parents and guardians can meet students in the visitor area during visiting hours after registering at the gate. Guests are not permitted inside rooms.
The exam schedule is published on the academic calendar and the student portal at least two weeks before the exams begin. Check the Examinations section for your semester's date sheet.

questions: How do I download my admit card?
Where can I get my admit card?
entries.answer: Admit cards are available on the student portal under Examinations about a week before the exams. You need cleared dues and the minimum attendance to download one. Carry a printout and your ID card to every exam.

questions: When will the results be declared?
How do I check my results?
Where can I see my marks?
entries.answer: Results are usually declared a few weeks after the last exam and are posted on the student portal. You can log in with your enrollment number to view and download your marksheet.

questions: What is the minimum attendance required?
What happens if I have an attendance shortage?
Can I sit in the exam with low attendance?
entries.answer: A minimum of 75 percent attendance is required to appear in the end-semester exams. Students with a shortage may be debarred unless they have an approved medical or special case, so submit documents to your department early.

questions: How do I apply for revaluation?
I am not happy with my result
entries.answer: You can apply for revaluation within a few days of the result by filling the form on the portal and paying the revaluation fee. The result of the revaluation is final.

questions: How do I clear a backlog?
What if I fail a subject?
entries.answer: If you fail a subject you can appear in the supplementary or reappear exam. Register for it on the portal within the notified window and pay the exam fee. Clearing backlogs early matters because many placement drives require none.

The placement cell invites companies across IT, core engineering and consulting each year. Training, mock interviews and aptitude sessions begin in the pre-final year, and year-wise placement statistics are published by the cell.

questions: What is the eligibility for placements?
Can students with backlogs sit for placements?
Do I need a minimum percentage to sit for placements?
entries.answer: Each company sets its own criteria, usually a minimum CGPA or percentage and no active backlogs. Register with the placement cell to see which drives you qualify for.

questions: How do I prepare for placements?
Can you help with my resume?
entries.answer: The placement cell runs aptitude training, coding practice, mock interviews and resume workshops. Start early, build projects, and practise problem solving regularly.

questions: Does the college help with internships?
How do I get an internship?
entries.answer: The placement cell shares internship openings and coordinates with companies. Many programs include a summer internship or industrial training, and your department can issue the required letters.

questions: How do I connect to the campus wifi?
entries.answer: Campus Wi-Fi is available in academic blocks, the library and hostels. Log in with your student ID and portal password. If it is not working, raise a ticket with the IT helpdesk.

questions: What food options are on campus?
Is there a mess or cafeteria?
Where can I eat on campus?
entries.answer: The campus has a central canteen and food courts serving breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner, with vegetarian options. The hostel mess serves meals at fixed timings.

questions: How do I reach the campus?
Is there a shuttle from the city?
entries.answer: College buses run on fixed routes from major city points, and registration is done through the transport office. Day scholars can also use public transport or cabs to reach the campus.

questions: Which games can I play on campus?
entries.answer: The campus has playing grounds, indoor courts and a gym. Students can join college teams and inter-college tournaments through the sports office.

questions: How do I join a club?
entries.answer: There are technical, cultural and literary clubs. Recruitment usually happens at the start of the semester, and clubs organise fests, hackathons and workshops through the year.

questions: Is there a medical facility on campus?
What do I do in a medical emergency?
entries.answer: A health centre on campus provides first aid and basic consultation, and an ambulance is available for emergencies. In an emergency, contact the security desk or your warden immediately.

questions: How do I get a duplicate ID card?
Where can I collect my ID card?
entries.answer: Submit a written request along with the duplicate ID fee at the administrative office. Lost cards should be reported to the department first.

questions: How can I contact the college?
Who do I contact for help?
entries.answer: Reach the student helpdesk through the Contact page on the college website, or visit the administrative block between 9:30 AM and 4:30 PM on working days.

questions: What topics do you know about?
entries.answer: I'm a campus helpdesk assistant. I can answer questions about admissions, fees, the library, hostel, exams, placements and day-to-day campus life. Try asking in your own words.

I'm built with classical NLP, not a pretrained LLM. I clean and spell-correct your question, match it against a knowledge base with TF-IDF and cosine similarity, classify its intent with Naive Bayes, and use a trigram language model as an experimental fallback.
